screened_primary_examples: Ramos & Schiestl 2019 Brassica rapa; Schiestl 2014 Brassica; Strauss et al. 1999 Brassica
decision: Resource reallocation is inferred from herbivory/pollination treatments or floral phenotype change; no joint A+D resource budget is measured.

screened_primary_examples: Stowe & Marquis 2010 Brassica defense-cost selection; Theis et al. 2014 Cucurbitaceae
decision: Defence investment can have fitness costs and A-D covariance can be tested, but neither identifies an additional cost of simultaneous flower A+D investment.

screened_primary_examples: Thosteman et al. 2024 Arabis alpina; Raphanus colour-glucosinolate architecture
decision: Integration/covariance tests evolutionary coupling and can be null even when physiological costs exist; foliar D also fails the strict organ gate.

screened_primary_examples: Manson et al. 2013 Delphinium nectar alkaloids; Manson et al. 2012 Asclepias nectar cardenolides
decision: Nectar secondary-metabolite allocation/transport costs are discussed but not directly measured, and no independent A axis is jointly costed.

screened_primary_examples: Stowe & Marquis 2010 Brassica; experimental-evolution defense-cost literature
decision: Direct costs of defence can be measured, but the defence is whole-plant/foliar and the cost is marginal D rather than A+D joint curvature.

screened_primary_examples: Liu et al. 2007 phenolic nectar; nectar sugar-saving studies
decision: Defensive nectar chemistry may maintain pollinator attraction at lower sugar reward and therefore suggest energy saving, but plant expenditure is not directly measured and D is not crossed with a distinct attraction axis.

screened_primary_examples: Armbruster et al. 2012 Dalechampia pollinator-resin reward cost
decision: Resin production has a directly manipulated pollinator-reward cost and resin has an ancestral defensive function, but reward and defence are functions of the same material rather than distinct A and D axes jointly costed.

screened_primary_examples: Lomatia floral cyanogenic-glycoside allocation; Nicotiana flower-specific jasmonate defence
decision: Flower-specific defence allocation is measured finely, but no attraction trait is jointly budgeted or costed.

screened_primary_examples: Thosteman et al. 2024 Arabis; Manson et al. 2012 Asclepias
decision: Chemical integration/allocation patterns do not measure intrinsic resource cost of producing both floral attraction and flower defence.
